paragraphs: In Ireland, anyone can call themselves a counsellor or a psychotherapist today. There are no legal rules for these jobs.
Now this will change. A state group called CORU is making new rules. After that, people without the right training cannot do this work.
Some therapist groups are not happy. They say the new rules ask for too few training hours. They also say therapists should have their own therapy too.
One group, with more than 7,000 members, sent a complaint to the European Commission.
The head of CORU, Claire O'Cleary, says the rules are only the minimum. She says people will be safer than now.

Counsellors and psychotherapists in Ireland will soon need to meet official standards for the first time. The new rules come from CORU, the group that controls health and social care jobs. After they start, it will be against the law to work in these jobs without the right qualifications.
The Government decided to act after an RTÉ Prime Time programme. It found that some unregulated counsellors had given poor and harmful advice to women at a difficult time in their lives.

CORU chief executive Claire O'Cleary says the rules are a minimum, not a limit. At the moment, people have no protection if something goes wrong, so she believes the public will be much safer.
